title: Claude Prompts showcase · design bible board
revision: board-07 · 2026-10-13 · references, laws, lineage, process (D56–D77); 24 owner-library cards with Eagle provenance; reads with creative-spec v4-brief-21 · §9 acting 2026-10-17
thesis: Raw capability is radiant and overwhelming; scaffolding is one lit join at a time. Saturated figures on a black field, Seuss architecture, Midnight Gospel shadows, drawn on twos with light on ones.
provenance: Every filed image's source, bytes and sha256 live in style-references.json and identity-references.json. Video cards keep a low-resolution private study copy next to this file; the href is the public original. Reference properties transfer, never figures or compositions. Nothing we have drawn is on this board: studies and their grades live under studies/ and are compared against this, never shown beside it.

roles.meaning: one darker step, a designed shape, graded by stipple (D47, D48)

timing.shape: nothing moves but boil and light
the move, one smear frame if far

rules: One actor moves at a time; related elements stagger 3–5 frames.
No linear curve anywhere: poses step, light springs with memory.
Boil is not shimmer: seeded variants at ~4/s, never a per-frame reseed.
Light lags drawing by 2–4 frames; glass lags light by 2–4 more.
Every move exposes cause and recovery; speed is never a move's identity.
No text moves. Identity pigments never grade.
The fewest cuts: beats progress by morphs and camera moves along leading lines the world provides (D64).
antireference: The early-web explainer video: everything tweening at once on a linear curve, hinge-jointed cutouts, pop-in text, no holds, no anticipation, motion with no cause.
Calm daylight scenery with fill everywhere and no negative space.
A frame interior that is a flat gradient, a picture instead of a place.
A toon shader standing in for drawn shadow shapes.
process: No asset enters a scene as its first iteration: a muse sheet of 3+ variants, each citing a card here, comes first (D55).
Two chains: showcase_preproduction once per episode, showcase_shot once per shot; the shot list is the handoff (D59).
A shot run feeds the script: measured ranges go back into shots.json and the beat (D60).
A render study is a frame set with probes, never one still (D61).
Blender is an explicit, confirmed, optional path on the render study (D62).
Companions keep their pigments and morph their construction to the world (D63).

Owner-library cards carry eagle://item/<ID> provenance and are filed through /inspiration; a reference cited anywhere in v3 without an id or URL is rejected by check-provenance (D74 fold, 2026-10-13).
medium: Remotion is the single substrate; the frame interior is a Three.js glass pass mounted through @remotion/three (D41).
This board holds references, laws and lineage only; nothing the project drew (D56).
No captions beyond the held title, planner assumption under D53 (D57).
Frame bars gold from the nested-frames painting, planner assumption (D58).

sections.title: 1 · World architecture
sections.law: The world inside the frame follows Dr. Seuss's Midnight Paintings: swooping organic towers, stacked pointed arches, curling stalks with flag leaves, pale thin contour outlines on a black field, light as beaded strings. The frame interior is receding hand-drawn frames, each slightly turned.

sections.title: 2 · Shadow, grain and the gadget
sections.law: Shadows are designed shapes: a form shadow following the silhouette and a cast shadow on the field, each with a weighted edge. Where a shadow grades it grades by two-scale stipple with a hue shift toward cool at contact, never a smooth ramp. The gadget is familiar parts in an impossible whole, like The Midnight Gospel's universe simulator.

sections.title: 3 · Field, palette and light
sections.law: Saturated figures on a black field, readable as negative space. Five roles per asset: a grayscale value pass first, then 2 mains, 1 shadow, 1 light, 1 accent. Identity pigments are separate from field pigments and never grade. One emitter per shot; radiance is additive and sits under the flat assets.

sections.title: 4 · Animation language: drawn on twos, light on ones
sections.law: The drawn layer (flat assets, contours, stipple) moves on twos with hold, anticipation, action, overshoot, settle, and boils visibly between seeded variants. The light layer (radiance, motes, glass, emitter) runs continuous on ones, lagging the drawing by 2–4 frames and recovering without snapping. Beats progress by cut and reframe, not pans.

sections.title: 5 · Cast and identity
sections.law: Original blue terminal-faced Codex and coral Clawd accompany the human from the opening. Their pigments are identity and never grade. No asset enters a scene as its first iteration: a muse sheet of 3+ variants, each citing a card on this board and one cast property, comes first.

sections.title: 7 · Colour script per shot (owner's CalArts picks)
sections.law: Each shot owns one hue pair and one emitter (D74): the radiance hue and one local accent, on the black field, with identity pigments untouched. The pair is chosen per shot from the owner's own CalArts saves, where a scene is one or two saturated colours as whole fields and the figure reads as a flat silhouette inside the light. Palette travel between shots is a cut or a morph on the chart, never a grey detour (C15).

sections.title: 8 · Camera and staging (owner's Composition picks)
sections.law: Every shot carries a cinematography sheet before its keys (D77): the frame at the start and end of the move, a top-down staging plan with the camera path, the leading line the move follows (D64), the emitter, the hue pair (D74) and the figure's on-screen height in heads. These cards are borrowed for framing and scale only: where the figure sits in the field, how a line leads the eye, how one emitter owns a frame.
